headline: PHP warned of a third remote code execution flaw two days after its emergency patches, as Mirai operators fired millions of failed exploit attempts at the first two and Hewlett Packard Enterprise closed eight maximum-severity ArubaOS bugs.

emerging_trends.text: Attackers increasingly skip the password entirely, replaying stolen Microsoft 365 sign-in sessions into mailboxes at 79 organizations and hiding inbox rules so victims never see parts of their own mail.

The week's worst bugs sit in the code that quietly decodes untrusted input, with Pillow handing an EPS filename to Ghostscript and Node.js unpacking crafted Brotli data, so one uploaded file reaches a shell.
emerging_trends.topic_title: Pillow and Node.js Decoders Run Attacker Code

emerging_trends.text: AI plumbing now carries its own attack surface and its own bill: attackers hijack exposed models to plan intrusions on the owner's compute, a default in the x402 SDKs let a malicious API drain an agent's token balance, and the leak site holding the AfD archive serves AI-written summaries of 421,179 stolen emails.

topics.title: PHP2Shell Draws Mass Mirai Scanning
topics.latest_developments: PHP disclosed a third remote code execution flaw, CVE-2026-115560, on October 23, 2026, two days after its emergency patches, saying it reaches only web applications configured in an unusual way and declining an emergency fix in favor of turning off the feature involved; SecurityWeek reported exploit code that bypasses address space layout randomization, researchers still confirm no successful compromise out of millions of attempts to enlist servers in the Mirai variant Potassium, and the SANS Internet Storm Center returned its InfoCon gauge to green Friday morning.
topics.summary: The pair of PHP flaws, each rated 9.2, give an unauthenticated attacker remote code execution on any PHP installation serving web requests, with the highest risk on Apache with mod_php and on PHP-FPM. Every site on PHP 8.2 through 8.5 needs the October 21, 2026 releases 8.5.12, 8.4.27, 8.3.36, and 8.2.35.

sources.title: PHP Warns of Another Unpatched RCE Two Days After Emergency PHP2Shell Patches
Mirai Botnet Operators Join PHP2Shell Attacks as ASLR Bypass Exploits Emerge
PHP Vulnerability Wrap-Up, (Fri, Oct 23rd)

topics.title: Capcom and Quest Diagnostics Count Victims
topics.latest_developments: Capcom, the Japanese gaming company, confirmed that a third party reached CAPCOM ID, the account service people use to sign in to its web services and play some of its games online, exposing more than 11.7 million customer email addresses and changing the login passwords on 196 accounts; Capcom spotted suspicious activity on October 19, 2026 and confirmed the intrusion the same day, and Quest Diagnostics told securities regulators that an intruder reached Quanum Lab Services Manager, the platform certain clients use to place test orders, and touched certain patient records.
topics.summary: Capcom account holders should expect phishing mail that imitates the company and should rotate any password they reused elsewhere. Quest Diagnostics has yet to put a number on the patient records involved.

topics.title: Third VeloCloud Orchestrator Zero-Day in Four Months
topics.latest_developments: SecurityWeek counted the actively exploited SQL injection flaw Arista Networks patched on October 22, 2026 as the third zero-day in VeloCloud Orchestrator in four months, a run that keeps handing attackers the management server for VeloCloud SD-WAN networks.
topics.summary: The critical flaw lets anyone who can log in to the orchestrator, even on a read-only customer account, reach privileged internal functionality and take operator privileges, the top level of control. Organizations running VeloCloud Orchestrator On-Prem should install Arista's updates and review orchestrator logins.

sources.title: Attackers Exploit Third VeloCloud Orchestrator Zero-Day in Four Months

topics.title: Pillow and Node.js Decoders Run Attacker Code
topics.latest_developments: Researchers disclosed CVE-2026-112900 in Pillow, the most widely used image library for Python, which passes an EPS file's name straight to Ghostscript and so runs whatever operating system command a caller buries in that name; Imperva published Node2Shell, a proof of concept that executed code on the official Node.js 24.22.0 image for Linux arm64 by feeding crafted data to the bundled Brotli decoder, CVE-2026-111497; and Atlassian's October bulletin listed 176 vulnerability entries, 14 of them critical, all in third-party components of its Data Center and Server products.
topics.summary: Pillow decodes uploaded images across Python web applications, so any server that opens an attacker-named EPS file hands over a shell, and the Node.js proof of concept needed no debugger or custom build. Teams running Pillow, Node.js, or Atlassian Data Center should install the current releases.

sources.title: Critical Flaw in Python’s Popular Pillow Image Library Allows Code Execution via a Crafted Image
Researchers Demonstrate Node2Shell RCE Exploit on Node.js Build Using Crafted Brotli Data

topics.title: Attackers Hijack Exposed AI Models and Agent Wallets
topics.latest_developments: Symantec researchers Priti More and Susmit Yenkar captured the instruction set of an attack tool that scans for AI models anyone on the internet can reach and then uses them to plan break-ins while the model's owner pays for the computing power, after its operators sent their entire working prompt to a honeypot posing as an unprotected AI service; the security firm V12 reported on October 22, 2026 that the default client in the x402 SDKs set no spending limit until the August 18 releases added one, so a malicious API could get an agent to sign a payment for its full balance of a supported token.
topics.summary: Both problems punish AI infrastructure left open by default: an unauthenticated model endpoint becomes an attacker's free hacking engine, and an agent that signs payments automatically becomes a wallet to empty. Operators should authenticate every model endpoint and set per-call spending caps on agent payment SDKs.

sources.title: Hackers hijack exposed AI models to launch cyberattacks at victims’ expense
Critical x402 SDK Flaw Could Let Malicious APIs Drain AI Agents’ Token Balances

topics.title: UK Weighs 14-Year Terms for Cable Sabotage
topics.latest_developments: The Department for Digital, Culture, Media and Sport published a White Paper this week proposing 14-year prison sentences for deliberately damaging undersea cables and pipelines off the British coast, plus unlimited fines for ship owners whose vessels cause the damage, superseding the Submarine Telegraph Act 1885 and its £1,000 maximum fine and five-year sentence.
topics.summary: Undersea cables carry nearly all intercontinental internet traffic, and the British law covering deliberate damage to them dates to 1885. Shipping companies and cable operators working in UK waters face new liability and penalties if Parliament adopts the plan.

sources.title: UK proposes 14-year prison terms for undersea cable sabotage
UK proposes 14-year jail terms for subsea cable saboteurs

topics.title: HPE Closes Eight Maximum-Severity ArubaOS Flaws
topics.latest_developments: Hewlett Packard Enterprise shipped updates on October 23, 2026 that fix 72 vulnerabilities in ArubaOS, among them eight maximum-severity authentication bypass and remote code execution flaws.
topics.summary: ArubaOS runs the controllers and gateways that carry enterprise Wi-Fi and branch networking, and an authentication bypass at that rating hands an unauthenticated attacker the device. Administrators should install the current ArubaOS builds and keep controller management interfaces off the public internet.

sources.title: HPE patches eight max severity RCE and auth bypass AOS flaws

topics.title: Microsoft 365 Session Replay Hits 79 Organizations
topics.latest_developments: Huntress reported on October 23, 2026 that one attacker spent ten weeks replaying stolen Microsoft 365 sign-in sessions against 79 organizations between July 14 and September 22, 2026, logging 497 successful sign-ins and more than 200,000 failed login attempts, planting hidden inbox rules that kept victims from seeing parts of their own mail, and running the replays from servers at the hosting provider 1337 Services GmbH.
topics.summary: A replayed session needs no password and no multi-factor code, so credential defenses miss it entirely. Security teams should revoke active sessions whenever they suspect a compromise, audit mailbox rules for hidden filters, and watch sign-ins from 1337 Services GmbH address space.

sources.title: Microsoft 365 accounts compromised at 79 organizations, no passwords needed

topics.title: 281 GB Leak Hits Germany's AfD
topics.latest_developments: The Alternative für Deutschland confirmed that hackers breached its hosting provider, and a leak site now offers 281 GB of party material, claims 421,179 internal party emails, and displays AI-written summaries in place of the messages themselves.
topics.summary: Germany's AfD lost its email archive through a vendor it does not run, the pattern that keeps turning political organizations into single points of failure. Verification of the trove remains open while the leak site shows only machine-written summaries.

sources.title: Hacker leaks 281 GB of data from Germany’s far-right AfD party

topics.title: Prince of Persia Moves a Server to US Hosting
topics.latest_developments: SecurityWeek reported on October 23, 2026 that the Iranian group Prince of Persia, after a three-month lull, hid a Tornado command-and-control server on United States shared hosting, its first server inside the country since 2016.
topics.summary: Prince of Persia runs the Tornado malware family and has long kept its control servers offshore. Defenders who weight suspicion by hosting geography will miss this infrastructure, since it now sits on domestic shared hosting alongside ordinary customer sites.

sources.title: Iran’s Prince of Persia APT Hosts C&C in US for First Time Since 2016

business_politics.title: Ukraine Says Starlink Remains Throttled
business_politics.latest_developments: Ukraine said Friday, October 23, that Starlink connections still fail when its drones fly at high speed, and Kyiv now accuses Washington of intentionally slowing the service, two days after President Trump telephoned Elon Musk and the link briefly appeared to run normally.
business_politics.summary: Ukrainian soldiers and government officials say the Starshield service their military runs on Starlink's standard equipment keeps dropping, degrading their ability to intercept Russian drones and strike targets inside Russia. Musk himself authorized the original restriction, Trump denies ordering it, and the outage sits at the center of the fight over how much Washington will keep underwriting Kyiv's defense.

business_politics.title: Brent Reaches $114 and European Gas Hits a 2022 High
business_politics.latest_developments: Brent reached $115 a barrel Friday, October 23, its highest since May, and the Dow slid as crude climbed; tight global fuel markets have driven refining margins to all-time highs, which makes refineries the swing factor in the oil majors' quarterly results, and European natural gas prices sit at their highest since late 2022.
business_politics.summary: Houthi attacks on Saudi energy infrastructure and the prospect of American strikes on Iran have pushed West Texas Intermediate above $101 and Brent to $115, and traders are pricing in the risk that renewed United States-Iran fighting cuts liquefied natural gas cargoes before winter. Eni opened the energy majors' earnings season Friday with an extraordinary dividend and a bigger buyback, while gold headed for a weekly loss of more than 3.5% as elevated energy costs revived inflation and rate-increase worries, and the dollar and Treasury yields both rose.

business_politics.title: Iran Threatens Economic and Civilian Targets
business_politics.latest_developments: Iran warned Friday, October 23, that it will widen its strikes to economic and civilian targets if the United States attacks, and Mike Waltz, President Trump's envoy, said Washington has prepared for a long stand-off and told Tehran it must reach a meaningful agreement on its nuclear program.
business_politics.summary: Tehran still holds large missile and drone stockpiles, and Washington has begun moving servicemembers and diplomatic staff out of range across the Gulf after the Houthi drone strike on Saudi Aramco's Shaybah oilfield. The standoff sits directly behind the five-month highs in crude and the 2022 highs in European gas.

business_politics.title: The AI Selloff Reaches Chip Listings and Pension Funds
business_politics.latest_developments: SK Hynix pulled the United States initial public offering of its memory-chip unit Solidigm on Friday, October 23, citing investor caution on artificial-intelligence valuations, and the Financial Times reported that Calpers cut its Magnificent Seven holdings; Nasdaq futures steadied after the index posted its worst day since June on Thursday.
business_politics.summary: The California Public Employees' Retirement System, the largest public pension fund in the United States, reduced its stakes in the seven biggest technology companies as doubts spread about lofty valuations and soaring capital spending, a retreat that follows Meta's disclosure that it will raise hundreds of billions of dollars for its artificial-intelligence buildout. Anthropic, meanwhile, struck a deal with the United Kingdom buyout group Hg to launch a European consultancy advising companies on deploying the technology.

business.title: Hellbender Records Presses Around the Vinyl Backlog
business.latest_developments: Pittsburgh City Paper reported Friday, October 23, that the Pittsburgh label Hellbender Records has partnered with the Irish pressing operation Anthem Vinyl.
business.summary: A global backlog at vinyl pressing plants has stretched the wait for independent labels to get records made, and Hellbender's arrangement with Anthem Vinyl gets its releases onto Pittsburgh turntables faster.

sources.title: Hellbender Records brings the luck of the Irish to Pittsburgh turntables

business.title: Westmoreland Buys Ads for Breeze Airways
business.latest_developments: Westmoreland County commissioners allocated $25,000 Thursday, October 22, to the county airport authority for an advertising campaign ahead of the Breeze Airways launch at Arnold Palmer Regional Airport.
business.summary: The county and the Westmoreland County Airport Authority committed more than $1.3 million in subsidies to bring Breeze Airways to the Latrobe airport under the deal the authority approved October 13, and the marketing money now goes toward filling those seats.

sources.title: Westmoreland County to fund ad campaign touting Breeze Airways launch at Arnold Palmer airport

business.title: Cupcake PGH Comes Full Circle in Allentown
business.latest_developments: Pittsburgh Magazine reported Friday, October 23, that Cupcake PGH has come full circle in the Allentown neighborhood of Pittsburgh.
business.summary: Amanda Baker, a service industry veteran and mother of four, began baking after her father died unexpectedly in 2022, credits the work with carrying her through major depression, and built the business out of a cottage kitchen.

sources.title: Cupcake PGH Comes Full Circle in Allentown

business.title: Peter Henry Takes the Kitchen at Scratch & Co.
business.latest_developments: Pittsburgh Magazine profiled Peter Henry on Friday, October 23, in his new job as executive chef of Scratch & Co.
business.summary: Henry wears his menu on his skin—asparagus over his heart, thyme, dill, tarragon, and garlic on his arms, turnips, beets, and corn on his legs—and now runs the kitchen at one of the city's longest-running farm-driven restaurants.

sources.title: Scratch & Co. Chef Peter Henry’s Passion for Food Is More Than Skin Deep

around_town.title: A Few State Senate Races Decide Harrisburg
around_town.latest_developments: The Post-Gazette laid out Friday, October 23, how a handful of Pennsylvania Senate races will settle control of the chamber, 11 days before the November 3 election.
around_town.summary: The Pennsylvania Senate holds the power to advance or bury Governor Josh Shapiro's agenda, and a small set of districts decides which party runs it. Western Pennsylvania's 46th District sits among the contested seats, where Republican Camera Bartolotta seeks a fourth term against Democrat Jodi Borello.

sources.title: How a handful of state Senate races could shape Pennsylvania's future

around_town.title: North Allegheny Ranks Second Among Area Districts
around_town.latest_developments: TribLive reported Friday, October 23, that Niche's 2027 rankings place North Allegheny School District second out of 77 districts in the Pittsburgh area, with North Hills communities also scoring high.
around_town.summary: Niche, the online ranking and review site, grades school districts and neighborhoods that home buyers and real estate agents across Allegheny County consult. North Allegheny serves the northern suburbs of the county.

sources.title: North Allegheny, North Hills communities score high in 2027 Niche rankings

around_town.title: Stackhouse Management Tenants Go Months Without Reliable Water
around_town.latest_developments: WTAE reported Thursday night, October 22, that residents of a Beaver County mobile home park have dealt with water problems for months, and the station found similar complaints at other Western Pennsylvania properties Stackhouse Management runs.
around_town.summary: Stackhouse Management operates manufactured-housing communities around the region, and its tenants in Beaver County say the water service has failed repeatedly without a fix.

sources.title: Residents frustrated by water issues at Beaver County mobile home park

around_town.title: Upper Burrell Adopts Its Data Center Ordinance
around_town.latest_developments: Upper Burrell Township supervisors voted unanimously Thursday, October 22, after a public hearing, to approve the zoning ordinance regulating data centers, two days after the township planning commission advanced it over the objections of residents who packed that meeting.
around_town.summary: The Westmoreland County township now has rules on the books governing where and how data centers may build, as developers press similar proposals in North Huntingdon, Connoquenessing in Butler County, and elsewhere across the region; residents at the hearing again raised concerns about the projects the ordinance would permit.

sources.title: Upper Burrell Township passes new zoning ordinance for data centers; residents express concerns

around_town.title: Pennsylvania Requires Disclosure on AI-Generated Ads
around_town.latest_developments: KDKA reported Thursday night, October 22, that Pennsylvania has become one of the first states in the country to require disclosures on advertisements generated with artificial intelligence.
around_town.summary: The statewide requirement lands 11 days before the November 3 election and follows the ordinance Allegheny County Council passed unanimously October 20 covering candidates for county office, after the gubernatorial campaign of Republican Stacy Garrity ran an AI-generated attack ad in Pennsylvania.

sources.title: Pennsylvania one of the first states to require disclosures on AI-generated ads
Pennsylvania has new law on AI-generated ads

around_town.title: Hempfield Revisits a Route 30 Gas Station
around_town.latest_developments: The Hempfield board of supervisors has taken up again the gas station proposed along Route 30, a month after a majority of the board rejected it.
around_town.summary: Neighbors objected that the Westmoreland County project sits too close to their homes, and that complaint sank the plan in September; the developer is back before the same supervisors.

sources.title: Proposed Gas station along Route 30 in Hempfield gets another look from supervisors

events.title: A Pizza Musical Casts the Audience
events.latest_developments: Pittsburgh City Paper previewed "Slice Something Slice" on Friday, October 23, an interactive musical about Pittsburgh pizza in which audience members take the starring role.
events.summary: The show grows out of the work of Dan Tallarico, the self-described pizza journalist who has reviewed Pittsburgh-area pizzerias through his blog Pizza Walk With Me, a Substack, and a newsletter, and who wrote a book on the subject; Tallarico argues the city punches above its weight on pizza.

sources.title: Bite into Slice Something Slice, a pizza musical where you’re the star

around_teams.title: Elliott Could Play a Year After His Injury
around_teams.latest_developments: The Post-Gazette reported Friday morning, October 23, that Steelers safety DeShon Elliott could return Sunday against the New Orleans Saints in Paris, a year removed from the injury the paper calls gruesome.
around_teams.summary: The Steelers ruled Elliott out of the October 18 game at the Tampa Bay Buccaneers, and his return would hand defensive coordinator Patrick Graham a starting safety back for the 9:30 a.m. Eastern kickoff Sunday, October 25, in a secondary already missing pieces.

sources.title: Steelers safety DeShon Elliott could return Sunday, a year removed from his gruesome injury

around_teams.title: Rodgers Would Back 16 Games Abroad in a Week
around_teams.latest_developments: The Post-Gazette reported Friday, October 23, that quarterback Aaron Rodgers said the NFL could stage 16 international games in a single week and that he would support the idea.
around_teams.summary: Rodgers made the case as the Steelers prepared to meet the New Orleans Saints in Paris on Sunday, October 25, the league's first regular-season game in France, one of the international dates the NFL keeps adding to the schedule.

sources.title: Aaron Rodgers says the NFL could play 16 international games in one week — and he’d support it

around_teams.title: The Steelers Fly Out for Paris
around_teams.latest_developments: The team's channel posted its departure videos, "Next stop: Paris" and "Bon voyage," early Friday, October 23, as the Steelers left for France, alongside a clip of Hall of Famers Dermontti Dawson and Mel Blount checking in from Paris on Thursday, October 22.
around_teams.summary: Pittsburgh meets the New Orleans Saints at 9:30 a.m. Eastern on Sunday, October 25, on NFL Network, and the team has filled the week with throwback highlights of running back Willie Parker and tight end Heath Miller against the Saints; defensive lineman Sebastian Joseph-Day stays home on injured reserve, with two rookie defensive linemen taking his snaps.
